Introduction

The goal of this project is to bring Linux to the Cassiopeia BE-300 PDA. If you are an end-user with little or no Linux experience, check the dummies section. Looking for porting/developing userland code for the BE running Linux, checkout the developers section. Want to get your hands dirty ? go straight to the hackers part.

07.01.03

Howto for dummies available

The 'dummies' section now contains easy instructions (and some screenshots) for novices to try the current Linux kernels on the BE-300. Alltough Linux is still far from being usable as a replacement for whatever is actually running on your BE, it allows you to play with it and show off ;-) Thanks to Baal (baal@megaoctet.net) for contributing this howto.

09.12.02

Update: progress report

The Linux4.BE gang has been hard at work. Jal0 has been hacking the BE hardware, mapping out the physical layout of the main board, creating schematics, and working on a monitor program (in CVS). Filip has made several discoveries while scanning various memory locations. Thanks to Filip's discoveries and help from themaw (Marc), I was able to write a simple scanning button driven keyboard driver (in CVS). Now you can activate the terminal and type to your heart's content. As always, there is still lots to be done and help is always welcome, even if you are not an experienced hacker.

06.11.02

uClibc/BusyBox ramdisk tutorial

I have written a tutorial that describes how to create an initial ramdisk based on uClibc and Busybox. It can be viewed here. UPDATE 12092002: I have added a follow-up tutorial on how to add PicoGUI to your ramdisk here.

# | 17.31 | jroark | three comments, already

Further progress booting kernel

I have been able to boot the kernel to the point that it calls init and starts busybox. However, there is still a lot of work to be done. We are experiencing what appears to be caching problems (the kernel only successfully boots uncached) and the serial driver is incomplete and unable to handle interupts properly. The latest fixes are in cvs. Thanks to Angus for the unaligned.c patch. Here are some links to a picture of the booting kernel and the current serial output.

08.07.02

Toolchain for Win32 (cygwin)

jal0 compiled the toolchain for win32 (cygwin), and wrote this howto. This will allow people using a win32 machine to build the kernel and userland applications without the need for a Linux box.
